memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He brought the burnt offering and offered it in the prescribed way." - Lev 9:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
In the prescribed way. Short verse, weighty phrase.

God had given a pattern, and Aaron followed it. Not because God is fussy about procedure, but because the pattern was itself a revelation. Every detail taught Israel something true about holiness, substitution, and access to God.

To improvise would have been to teach something false.

The same is true of the gospel. There is a prescribed way to God, and it is not narrow-mindedness to say so. Jesus said, I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me (Jn 14:6). Peter told the Sanhedrin, Salvation is found in no one else (Acts 4:12).

We live in a time that finds such claims uncomfortable. But consider the alternative. If there were no prescribed way, every person would be left guessing, and no one could ever be sure. The prescription is not a barrier. It is a kindness.

God did not leave us to invent our own route to Him. He made one and told us where it is.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I trying to approach God on terms I have devised rather than the ones He gave?
2. Does the exclusivity of Christ trouble me, or reassure me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You did not leave me guessing how to reach You. I come by the way You have provided, through Christ. Amen.
